sections.html:
Madison County's seat, Anderson, lies in east-central Indiana roughly 40 miles from Indianapolis. The city covers 41.71 square miles, and the White River crosses its northern part from east to west. Anderson Township holds most of it, and slivers belong to Adams, Fall Creek, Lafayette, Richland and Union townships. The city had 54,788 people in 2020 after peaking at 70,787 in 1970.

Five ZIP codes serve the city: 46011, 46012, 46013, 46016 and 46017. Communities such as Country Club Heights, Edgewood, River Forest and Woodlawn Heights sit outside the city limits, which means a house with an Anderson mailing address might not be under city code enforcement at all.

sections.h2: Why so many Anderson houses are older
sections.html:
Natural gas found on March 31, 1887 set off the Indiana gas boom and made Anderson a factory town. Glassmaking and other gas-fed industries arrived, and when the gas ran out in 1912 several plants left. Rubber, auto parts and lighting kept the city going. Delco Remy and Guide Lamp were its top two employers for decades, and about 22,000 people worked for General Motors in Anderson in the 1970s. By 2006 that number was under 2,600.

Many of the houses were built for that plant workforce. When an owner starts thinking about selling, the talk usually turns to age and deferred maintenance. A hot July and a cold January test roofs and furnaces, and repeated freezing and thawing wears on old plumbing and masonry. A cash buyer prices those repairs into an offer on a house taken in its current state.

Most of Anderson belongs to Anderson Community School Corporation: Anderson High School, Highland Middle School, six elementary schools, a kindergarten center and a preschool. South Madison Community School Corporation serves a small part, and Anderson Preparatory Academy is a charter school with no tuition. Confirm a parcel's district before telling a buyer which schools it feeds.

State Road 32 is 14th Street through the center and runs about 19 miles northeast to Muncie and 19 miles southwest to Noblesville. State Road 9, or Scatterfield Road, goes about 11 miles north to Alexandria and 10 miles southwest to Pendleton. Interstate 69 clips the southeast corner at Exit 226, and Fort Wayne is 83 miles away.

Code enforcement and inspections belong to the city's Department of Municipal Development, at 120 E. Eighth Street, open weekdays 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. It administers building codes in existing structures, assesses soundness and habitability, and can require owners to repair a house or remove hazards. If a structure is judged unsafe, occupants must leave.

In an emergency the city works with public safety departments to board, seal or fence an unsafe structure, and the owner pays those costs. Reports come in by phone at 765-648-6055 or through the Report a Concern tracker on the city website. Vacant and neglected houses draw the most attention, so a seller holding one should resolve open notices before closing.

Taxes on an Anderson house go to Madison County, with the spring installment due in May. Payment options:

  • At the Government Center counter on weekdays, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.
  • Mailed to the Treasurer, 16 E. 9th St, Room 109, Anderson, IN 46016, along with your original coupon.
  • Online, at $1.95 for an e-check or 2.95 percent for a card.
  • By phone at 765-204-9553, with a 95 cent fee.

State caps hold homestead tax to 1 percent of gross assessed value, other residential property to 2 percent and commercial property to 3. Challenge a value with Form 130, generally due June 15 for the current assessment, and check any number with the county before relying on it.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works in Anderson
sections.html:
There are only a few steps. First you describe the house to us: address, condition and any work you know it needs. We review it and send an offer. Accept, and you pick the closing date at a local title company. With no lender involved, there is no loan approval to collapse at the last minute.

The title company takes on the paperwork. It searches title, prepares the closing statement, settles the mortgage and any open tax out of your proceeds, and records the deed. An estate house means it will request the documents showing who is allowed to sign.

Typical Anderson sellers include heirs with a house in an older neighborhood, landlords with a worn-out rental, owners of vacant houses that draw city notices, and people who cannot pay for repairs a lender would demand. The house is bought as it is, so there is nothing to paint, patch or haul away first.

Timing is yours to set within reason. Closing depends mostly on how quickly the title company finishes its search and paperwork, so tell us early if you need a particular date or are moving out of town.

Before you accept, compare the offer with what listing would leave you after repairs, showings, carrying costs and the time the house sits. Ask how long closing will take, what the title company charges and who pays each fee, and get the answers in writing.

sections.h2: What to settle before selling an Anderson house
sections.html:
Gather the paperwork that tells a buyer what they are inheriting:

  • The latest tax bill and a payoff for any open installment.
  • Any code enforcement notice or open permit from the city.
  • Proof of who may sign, such as a deed, estate papers or power of attorney.
  • A list of known repairs, such as roof, furnace, plumbing and foundation.

Sellers who list on the open market handle showings and repairs, and those who sell as-is to a cash buyer trade some price for speed and certainty. Neither route is wrong. The better one depends on how much work the house needs, how long you can carry it and what you owe on it.

A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and loan underwriting, so a house with repair needs is not held up by a financing condition. You send the address and a description of the condition, review the offer, and if you want it you pick a closing date with a local title company. The title company pays off any mortgage or tax balance from your proceeds, and you receive what is left.

If a code notice is open, tell the buyer at the start. The city may still require repairs or hazard removal after the sale, and a buyer who learned about it late is more likely to reprice or withdraw. Ask Municipal Development what is outstanding, and keep the written answer with your closing papers.

faqs.q: Is Anderson, Indiana, in Madison County?
faqs.a: Yes. Anderson is the county seat of Madison County and its largest city.

faqs.q: Who handles code enforcement in Anderson?
faqs.a: The Department of Municipal Development, at 120 E. Eighth Street. Call 765-648-6055 or use the city's Report a Concern tracker.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Madison County property tax?
faqs.a: In person at the Madison County Government Center, by mail to 16 E. 9th St, Room 109, Anderson, online, or by phone. Online and phone payments carry fees.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Anderson house that has code violations?
faqs.a: Yes. Buyers can purchase a house with open issues, but the city may still require repairs or hazard removal. Tell the buyer about every notice and ask the department what is outstanding.

faqs.q: Which school district is Anderson in?
faqs.a: Most of the city is in Anderson Community School Corporation. A small part is in South Madison Community School Corporation, so confirm the address.
